summary: Backend-only verification of FASE 1 ampliada (attendance push migration to device_tokens + per-role routing). The critical routing pytest (tests/test_attendance_push_targets.py) PASSES — validates alumno->S1+P1+P2, profesor->T1, dedupe, exclusion of inactive tokens/other students, and send_attendance_push without tokens returns (0,0). Added a new pytest module test_attendance_push_migration.py (6 tests, all passing) covering: (a) send_attendance_notification no longer references db.push_tokens and delegates FCM to send_attendance_push; (b) the QR scan flow has >=2 'await send_attendance_push(' calls (teacher entry + exit branches); (c) save_student/teacher/maintenance_attendance schedule the push via asyncio.create_task(_push_attendance_batch(..., rol)) so the HTTP response is NOT blocked; (d) parent_notifications row is still created for the parent on QR student ingreso (no-regression); (e) _push_attendance_batch dedupes user_ids and swallows exceptions (errors are logged); (f) send_fcm_to_devices supports data_only kwarg (data-only push with playSound). HTTP-level save endpoints were also probed for non-regression — all 4 endpoints return HTTP 403 with the subscription-suspended message for the elroble admin (expected, not a bug); routes exist and middleware behaves consistently.
action_items: OPTIONAL: provide credentials for a colegio with ACTIVE subscription so a future HTTP-level smoke test of POST /api/attendance/{students,teachers,maintenance}/save can be exercised end-to-end (current elroble + 'los gatos' both 403 via subscription middleware for the provided admin/teacher accounts). Validation via the routing+migration pytest is sufficient for this iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/notifications.py: send_attendance_notification now delegates FCM to send_attendance_push (line ~337) and falls back gracefully when no parents are found (line ~237). The legacy /api/notifications/test endpoint (~L350-L410) still uses db.push_tokens — this is explicitly out of scope per the request and is harmless.

routes/attendance.py: import of send_attendance_push is wrapped in try/except with a (0,0)-returning fallback (L36-L41) — robust against circular import. _push_attendance_batch (L50-L61) dedupes via dict.fromkeys, fetches names with a single $in query, and catches per-user exceptions so a single bad token cannot abort the batch. Hooks land in save_student (L456), save_teacher (L1223), save_maintenance (L1346) and the two QR teacher branches (L2589/L2642). All saved endpoints use asyncio.create_task -> response is NEVER awaited on the push.

POTENTIAL ENHANCEMENT (not a bug): _push_attendance_batch iterates user_ids sequentially with await send_attendance_push. For very large batches (>200 students saved at once) this could be parallelized via asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True). Current behavior is still non-blocking for the HTTP response because the whole batch is scheduled via create_task; only kept as a follow-up.

POTENTIAL ENHANCEMENT (not a bug): send_attendance_push currently does NOT pass the 'rol' value into the FCM data payload (only into the log line). If the SW/clients ever need to differentiate sound/icon by role, expose rol in the data dict.

success_rate.backend: 100% (7/7 tests pass: 1 routing + 6 migration). HTTP save endpoints unreachable due to subscription suspension on the only available test schools — not a bug; routes exist and return 403 consistently as expected.

seed_data_creation: Only ephemeral test-school + test-users + test-device_tokens documents created inside the pytest scenarios; all deleted in finally blocks. No persistent test data left in the DB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Re-running: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_attendance_push_targets.py tests/test_attendance_push_migration.py -v` — both files together pass (7/7). The migration test re-binds routes.notifications.db / routes.attendance.db to a fresh AsyncIOMotorClient inside the single asyncio.run() so it works after the routing test's loop is closed in the same pytest session — this pattern can be reused when adding more async DB tests against the shared Motor client. If you ever need to HTTP-test the save endpoints, you must first find or create a colegio with subscription_status='active' AND no other suspension flags (the two existing schools show subscription_status='active' in the DB but the middleware still blocks — there is an additional suspension signal not surfaced in the schools doc; consider checking /api/auth/me / /api/schools/{id}/subscription for the actual suspension source).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bug to RCA. This iteration is a non-regression + migration verification. The migration from db.push_tokens -> db.device_tokens + per-role routing (alumno=self+padres, profesor/personal=self only) is correctly implemented and the response of the save endpoints is non-blocking (asyncio.create_task).
